requirements.requirement: Repair /srv/legacy2/child-process-reaping/supervisor.py so each invocation starts exactly the requested number of short jobs, records every job's exit status, uses status 0 for even-numbered jobs and 3 for odd-numbered jobs, and preserves existing results.
requirements.summary: Runs requesting 6, 4, and 8 jobs produced exactly 6, 4, and 8 new records with no parity/status errors. The original previous,0,0 record remained present, including after reboot. The repaired script persisted at the required location.

requirements.requirement: The supervisor must remain active until its children finish and reap every child rather than leaving zombies.
requirements.summary: The implementation tracks every forked PID and loops on os.wait() until the child map is empty. Completed runs returned only after all requested result rows were recorded, and direct checks after pre- and post-reboot runs found zero zombie processes.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed legacy operating-system release and kernel, using compatible software.
requirements.summary: The repaired script compiled and executed with Python 2.5.1. The node remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic after the repair and restart; lifecycle platform observations also show the same kernel before and after execution.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for the sole managed node: a healthy pre-restart functional state was captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed consistently with the fixed lifecycle observations, and post-restart execution confirmed recovered code, preserved data, correct statuses, and zero zombies.
limitations: Zombie checks were point-in-time, system-wide observations after completed runs rather than PID-specific tracing throughout execution; the wait loop and complete result sets provide coherent supporting evidence.
Failed-service lifecycle collection was unsupported because this legacy platform lacks systemctl, although the task did not introduce or require a managed service.
The final evidence does not inventory the task directory for possible generated bytecode such as supervisor.pyc, so absence of that minor build artifact cannot be confirmed.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Required mutations were narrowly scoped: replacing supervisor.py, appending bounded verification runs to results.tsv, creating temporary safety/build files, and rebooting for the mandatory restart protocol. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred: cmd-a89e37da055649df executed the known-broken original supervisor with four jobs but captured no diagnostic state that contributed to the repair. That experiment was transient—the process completed—and no associated final residue is shown. Final lifecycle checks found no added temporary files, listening sockets, or package-health regression.
